differential.name: Diabetic nephropathy progression
differential.rationale: Chronic hyperglycemia with microalbuminuria and CKD stage 2 suggests worsening diabetic kidney disease as the primary driver of rising creatinine.

differential.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis
differential.rationale: Long‑standing essential hypertension in a patient with CKD and controlled electrolytes fits chronic pressure‑related renal injury.

differential.name: Acute tubular necrosis (ischemic)
differential.rationale: Sudden rise in serum creatinine (1.9 mg/dL) on a CKD background may reflect an acute insult such as volume depletion or hypotension.

differential.name: Acute interstitial nephritis (drug‑induced)
differential.rationale: Recent medication changes (medication review due) and CKD predispose to AIN, which can acutely worsen renal function.

differential.name: Metastatic breast cancer involving the kidney
differential.rationale: History of malignant breast neoplasm raises the possibility of renal metastases contributing to renal impairment, though less common.
